I think I might be gluten intolerant after all of the recent focus on grain. Fun discussion last night, with a few takeaways — the retrospectively bizarre one being the progression of Genghis Khan → Sapiens → Against the Grain. Not planned, but an interesting run of related topics.
Inventing the Renaissance takes December.
A clean win at the top for once — and the tie moved down to second, where an even 4–4 head-to-head forced the fall-through to first-place votes.
All — eight of you ranked nine candidates this round. Inventing the Renaissance (Palmer) took it on 54 points, six clear of the field, and reads December. No tiebreaker was needed for the win; the drama was one row lower.

§ About that tie
Say Nothing and Something Rich and Strange both finished on 48 points. The methodology calls for a Condorcet head-to-head first: ignore the rest of the ballot and ask how each voter ranked these two against one another.
Head-to-head
Say Nothing 4 · Something Rich and Strange 4
The head-to-head split 4–4 — dead even, no winner, nothing to separate them. That sends the tie through to the next breaker, first-place votes, where Say Nothing leads 2–1 and takes second. Both books stay on the candidate list at full strength.
